talks.title: X-Hour Film Contest: Xploit
talks.teaser: An original sci-fi short film conceived, shot, and edited in 48 hours during DEF CON 22 by TooSmartGuys for the X-Hour Film Contest.
talks.summary:
### 48-Hour Film Production: Xploit
At 00:16, the short film opens on two collaborators troubleshooting a malfunctioning piece of hardware, struggling to power the device before attempting an alternate configuration. Produced for the DEF CON 22 X-Hour Film Contest, the creative project challenged teams to conceive, film, and edit a complete narrative short within a strict 48-hour time constraint during the convention.

### Hacker Narrative and Cinematic Experimentation
At 01:28, the protagonists execute their technical improvisation amidst escalating tension. Created by production duo TooSmartGuys, the piece exemplifies the convergence of filmmaking, technology, and underground culture within DEF CON's artistic contest tracks.

talks.title: X-Hour Film Contest Winner: Invasion of the Bboonians
talks.teaser: The winning short film from the DEF CON 22 X-Hour Film Contest, written, shot, and edited in 48 hours by team Uberlab.
talks.summary:
### TD Francis X-Hour Film Contest Winner
At 00:00, team Uberlab presents *Invasion of the Bboonians*, the winning entry for the inaugural TD Francis X-Hour Film Contest at DEF CON 22. Teams were tasked with creating, filming, and editing an original sci-fi short film within 48 hours amidst the conference.

### Sci-Fi Spoof and Conference Creativity
At 00:45 and 01:20, the short film delivers a humorous sci-fi parody chronicling an encounter with extraterrestrial invaders, combining campy practical effects with fast-paced editing. The project captures hacker culture's creative community traditions and guerrilla filmmaking during DEF CON.

talks.title: X-Hour Film Contest: Brian Knappenberger Announces Winner
talks.teaser: Documentary filmmaker Brian Knappenberger announces the winning entry and judges''' selections for the DEF CON 22 X-Hour Film Contest.
talks.summary:
Announcing the X-Hour Film Contest Winner

Documentary filmmaker Brian Knappenberger (director of "We Are Legion" and "The Internet's Own Boy") addresses DEF CON 22 attendees to celebrate the inaugural TD Francis X-Hour Film Contest.

Celebrating Hacker Cinema and Creativity

Seven competitive teams produced original short science fiction films over the conference weekend. Knappenberger highlights the humor, inventive practical effects, and chaotic energy of the submissions, officially announcing the Uber Lab team as the contest winners for their comedic film "Invasion of the Boonians."

talks.title: FTC Zapping Rachel Robocall Contest Update
talks.teaser: FTC Commissioner Terrell McSweeny and Patricia Hsue share updates on the Zapping Rachel contest challenging hackers to build robocall blocking solutions.
talks.summary:
Combating Illegal Automated Robocalls

Representatives from the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) provide an update on the "Zapping Rachel" crowdsourcing contest at DEF CON 22. The initiative mobilized the security research community to develop innovative technological countermeasures against illegal automated telemarketing robocalls.

Contest Tracks and Technical Challenge Goals

The challenge tasked competitors with building analytical honeypots, caller ID spoofing detectors, and telephony filtering systems capable of identifying and disrupting automated call distribution networks used by deceptive telemarketers.

Crowdsourcing Defensive Telecommunications Innovations

The briefing highlights winning solutions submitted by security researchers, demonstrating how algorithmic pattern analysis, carrier-level signaling verification, and automated honeypots can empower regulators and consumers to combat widespread telemarketing fraud.
